=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/review_sweep_round_cap.sh:164 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: The round count filter (`$created >= $since[.]`) uses the head commit's committer date, not the push date, so review runs created before a late push are excluded from the cap.
  WHY: This can make the cap inert for PRs that are pushed after local commits and review runs. The reviewer rated it NIT, confidence 4.
- scripts/review_autofix_step_evaluate_gate.sh:1385 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: The author identity check (`pr_author_login != gate_marker_author_login`) is case-sensitive, though GitHub logins are treated as case-insensitive.
  WHY: A login that differs only in case could wrongly reject the generated-chore exemption.
- scripts/review_sweep_round_cap.sh:199-205 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: The escalation comment write (line 199) is not idempotent, while the label write (line 205) uses `gh_api_retry --idempotent`.
  WHY: If the comment succeeds and the label write fails, the next sweep tick posts a duplicate comment.
- changelog.d/9683-review-round-cap-and-generated-chore-skip.md:2 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The headline states the cap unconditionally ("after 10 review rounds in 48 hours"), but the shipped rule (scripts/review_sweep_round_cap.sh:164 and scripts/review_sweep_head_gate.sh:118) counts only rounds since the PR's current head commit's committer date, and line 4 of the same file says so.
  WHY: An operator reading only the headline expects escalation at 10 rounds. PRs whose head keeps moving through `[ai-merge-resolve]` commits or base-sync `update-branch` merges are never escalated.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
- requirement: "A PR whose head is not approved (head_gate_state present and not success) and that has SWEEP_REVIEW_MAX_ROUNDS (default 10) or more rounds in the last SWEEP_REVIEW_ROUND_WINDOW_HOURS (default 48) is not dispatched." (PR description). The google reviewer quoted it as 10 or more rounds in the last 48 hours.
  expected_change_site: scripts/review_sweep_round_cap.sh, review_sweep_round_counts (per-PR cutoff at lines 102-121, count filter at line 164)
  confidence=5
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna]
  EVIDENCE: scripts/review_sweep_round_cap.sh lines 102-121 and 164 count only runs created at or after the PR's current head commit's committer date (`$created >= $since[.]`), so rounds from earlier heads are excluded even within the window, and the PR description does not state this head-move reset. Severity disagreement: google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite and openai_gpt-6-luna rated it MAJOR, minimax_minimax-m3 rated it NIT. The narrowing is documented in the changelog, README and agents fragment.
=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===
- scripts/review_sweep_round_cap.sh:164 | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The round count logic (`$created >= $since[.]`) filters out review runs created before the PR's current head commit (`head_committed_at`).
  WHY: `head_committed_at` is the committer date, not the push date, so review runs made on a locally committed fix before it is pushed are not counted. This makes the cap inert for PRs that are being actively pushed to.
- scripts/review_autofix_step_evaluate_gate.sh:1385 | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The author identity check (`pr_author_login != gate_marker_author_login`) is case-sensitive, while GitHub logins are treated as case-insensitive.
  WHY: A login that differs only in case could wrongly reject the generated chore PR exemption.
- scripts/review_sweep_round_cap.sh:205 | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The label write uses `gh_api_retry --idempotent`, but the comment write just before it (line 199) has no idempotency guard.
  WHY: If the comment write succeeds and the label write fails, the next sweep tick posts the comment again, creating duplicates.
- TASK_GAP:
  Requirement: The PR description states that the sweep cap applies to "10 or more rounds in the last 48 hours" as an unconditional per-PR bound.
  Expected change site: The logic in `scripts/review_sweep_round_cap.sh` and `review_sweep_round_counts`.
  Evidence of absence: The code counts only rounds created since the PR's current head commit (`$created >= $since[.]`, where `$since` is `head_committed_at`), so rounds from an earlier head are excluded even within the window. The PR description does not state this reset-on-head-move behavior.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
=== END FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- changelog.d/9683-review-round-cap-and-generated-chore-skip.md:2 | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The headline states the cap unconditionally, while the shipped rule (scripts/review_sweep_round_cap.sh:164, scripts/review_sweep_head_gate.sh:118) counts only rounds created at or after the current head commit's committer date. Line 4 of the same file states the narrower rule, so the file contradicts itself.
  WHY: A PR whose head moved inside the window never reaches the limit. scripts/review_autofix_step_count_iterations.sh:95-131 counts only `[ai-autofix]`/`[claude-autofix]` commits, and `[ai-merge-resolve]` commits (scripts/review_conflict_prepare.sh:580,802) and base-sync merges (scripts/pr_checks_lib.sh:1494) reset the count floor without counting toward any cap. Such a PR is never escalated, so the headline overstates the protection.
- TASK_GAP:
  Requirement: "A PR whose head is not approved (head_gate_state present and not success) and that has SWEEP_REVIEW_MAX_ROUNDS (default 10) or more rounds in the last SWEEP_REVIEW_ROUND_WINDOW_HOURS (default 48) is not dispatched." (PR description, section 1)
  Expected change site: scripts/review_sweep_round_cap.sh, review_sweep_round_counts (per-PR cutoff at lines 102-121, count filter at line 164)
  Evidence of absence: The helper builds a per-PR cutoff from the head commit's committer date (lines 105-109) and keeps a run only when `$created >= $since[.]` (line 164), so rounds against an earlier head are excluded within the 48-hour window. The narrowing is documented in the helper header (lines 26-38), the README, the agents fragment and the changelog, but not in the PR description. The reviewer called the gap description-only: the code needs no change.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
- HARDENING_SUGGESTIONS: scripts/review_sweep_round_cap.sh, jq count filter at line 164 (`--jq` projection at line 140). The 48-hour window is enforced only by the API-side `created>=` parameter. Suggested fix: pass `--arg cutoff "${cap_cutoff}"` and add `and ($created >= $cutoff)` to the `select(...)` on line 164 (about 2 lines). HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 1
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
